title: Sign in and find your content
goal: Open the CMS and choose the area you want to edit.
steps: Open the private CMS address supplied with your editor account. Enter your email and password, then click Log in.
Choose Projects in the left sidebar for portfolio work, Pages for the fixed text pages, or Site Settings for site wide details.
In Projects or Pages, use Search to find an item. Click its row to open the editor.
Use Back to table to return to the full list.
check: The selected item opens with its fields and save controls.
notes: The training recordings use a local copy and example credentials. Use your own editor account on the real CMS.
The CMS has no public sign up or password reset control on this screen. Ask the site administrator for access or password help.

chapters.text: To sign in, open the private CMS address provided with your editor account. Enter your email and password.
Click Log in. The left sidebar separates Projects, Pages, and Site Settings.
Choose Projects. Use the search box to find a work, then click its row to open the editor.
The item fields appear on the right. Back to table returns to the full list.

title: Add a project
goal: Create a new portfolio entry and prepare it for review.
steps: Choose Projects, then New Project. A new empty record is created immediately.
Enter Title, Year, and Medium. Put separate materials or dimensions on separate lines in Medium.
Review the generated Slug. Fill in optional subtitles, original title, language code, and Description as needed.
Add a Hero image. Add gallery images if the work needs additional views.
Click Save to keep a draft. When the required fields are complete, use Queue to publish, then Publish site when you are ready to release the changes.
check: The project has the intended title and images. Its status remains Not published until it is queued and published.
notes: Title, Slug, Year, Medium, Hero, and the internally managed position are required when publishing. Incomplete drafts can be saved.
Creating a record is immediate. Discarding field edits does not remove the new record. Delete an unused empty draft separately.

chapters.text: To add a project, open Projects and click New Project. This creates an empty draft straight away.
Enter the title, year, and materials. The slug follows the title while it is new. Check the address before saving.
Add a description if needed. Then choose a Hero image, which represents the work on the website.
Wait for image optimisation to finish. Click Save to store the draft and upload the selected image.
The work is saved as Not published. Use Queue to publish when it is complete, then follow the separate publishing procedure.

title: Edit project text and its address
goal: Update a work without losing track of its website address.
steps: Open the project and edit Title, Year, Medium, Subtitle, or original title fields.
Use Description for the text shown with the work. Select text and use the toolbar for headings, bold, italic, lists, and links.
Review Slug only if you intend to change the URL. Existing saved slugs do not follow later title changes.
Click Save. If the item was Published, saving changed content queues it for publishing. Publish the site to release it.
check: Unsaved disappears and the saved text remains when you reopen the item.
notes: Changing a slug changes the project address. Existing links may stop working; there is no redirect editor in this CMS.
The slug link points to the public website. It is not a preview of unsaved changes.

chapters.text: To edit a work, open its record and change the relevant text fields.
The Description toolbar supports formatted text. Select words before applying bold, italic, headings, or a list.
An existing saved slug stays the same when you rename a work. Change the slug only when you intend to change its web address.
Click Save. Changes to a published item are queued. Publish the site when the update is ready.

title: Replace a project image
goal: Change a Hero image or another single image field.
steps: Open the project and scroll to Hero, Thumb, or Social image.
Click Replace beside an existing image, then select the new file. Empty image fields accept a file by clicking the drop area or dropping a file onto it.
Wait for Optimising to finish. Pending upload means the file is staged in this browser and has not yet been uploaded.
Click Save or Queue to publish. Wait for the upload to finish before leaving. Publish the site when ready.
check: The new thumbnail appears and Pending upload is gone after saving.
notes: Hero is required to publish. Thumb is optional and falls back to Hero when empty. Social image also falls back to Hero for projects.
For an optional single image, Delete clears that field; save the record to keep the change. It does not delete the project.
The CMS normally optimises raster images to a maximum long edge of 1920 pixels and checks a 4 MB upload limit. Keep original master images separately.

chapters.text: To replace a project image, open the work and scroll to Hero. Click Replace and select the new file.
The CMS optimises the file first. Pending upload means it is still staged locally in this browser.
Click Save to upload and attach the replacement. Wait until saving finishes.
The new thumbnail is now saved. Publish the site to update the live image. Optional Thumb and Social image fields work the same way.

title: Add images to a gallery
goal: Add extra views to a project in viewing order.
steps: Open the project and scroll to Gallery.
Click the gallery drop area and select one or more files, or drag image files onto it.
Wait for optimisation. Review the new rows, image names, and thumbnails.
Click Save to upload the staged files. Use the separate reorder and caption procedures as needed, then publish when ready.
check: The new gallery rows remain when the project is reopened and no longer show Pending upload.
notes: The gallery accepts multiple files and allows up to 200 images by default. Add large sets in manageable batches.
Gallery images and Hero are separate fields. Adding a gallery image does not replace Hero.

chapters.text: To add more views of a work, open its Gallery field.
Click the drop area and select your image files. You can also drag files onto this area.
Wait for optimisation. Each added file appears as a gallery row with a thumbnail and an optional caption.
Click Save to upload the images. Check that Pending upload disappears, then publish the site when ready.

title: Add or change a gallery caption
goal: Write the text displayed beneath a gallery image.
steps: Open the project and scroll to Gallery.
Find the correct image using its thumbnail and file name.
Paste the complete caption into Caption optional beneath that image. Clear the field to remove a caption.
Click Save, then publish the site when ready.
check: The saved caption is attached to the intended image. After deployment, it appears beneath that image on the project page.
notes: Reordering an image carries its caption with it. Check the image itself rather than relying only on its current row number.
In this version, typing a caption can remove spaces. Pasting the complete caption preserves internal spaces.

chapters.text: To add a gallery caption, find the image by its thumbnail and file name.
Click Caption optional beneath that image and paste the complete caption. This preserves spaces in the current version.
Click Save. Clearing this same field removes the caption without removing the image.
Publish the site when ready, then check the caption beneath the correct image on the project page.

title: Reorder gallery images
goal: Change the sequence of images within one project.
steps: Open the project and scroll to Gallery.
Drag the grip on an image row to its new position. Drop at the insertion line.
For keyboard control, focus the same grip and press Arrow Up or Arrow Down.
Review the sequence from top to bottom, click Save, then publish the site.
check: The saved gallery sequence matches the intended order and each caption stays with its image.
notes: This changes the order inside one project. Use the project list to change the order of works across the portfolio.

chapters.text: To change the image sequence within a project, use the grip at the left of a Gallery row.
Drag the image to its new position and release at the insertion line. The caption moves with the image.
You can also focus an image grip and press the up or down arrow key to move it one position.
Review the sequence, click Save, and publish the site to make the gallery order live.

title: Remove an image from a gallery
goal: Remove one gallery entry while keeping the project.
steps: Open the project and scroll to Gallery.
Locate the image by its thumbnail and file name.
Click its Remove button at the right of the row. Check that the correct row disappears.
Click Save to keep the removal, then publish the site. Use Discard before saving if you removed the wrong image.
check: The intended image is absent from the saved gallery and the remaining images are in the right order.
notes: The gallery Remove button has no confirmation dialog. The change is still a local edit until you save.
Removing an image entry does not delete the whole project or offer a media library cleanup command.

chapters.text: To remove one gallery image, find the correct thumbnail and file name.
Click the Remove button at the right of that row. The image disappears from the gallery immediately.
Check the remaining images before clicking Save. If you removed the wrong one, Discard restores the last saved record.
After saving, publish the site to remove the image from the live project page.

title: Reorder projects
goal: Change the order of works across the portfolio.
steps: Choose Projects and return to the full table. Clear Search and leave Select mode if either is active.
Drag the grip at the far left of a project row to its new position. Use the insertion line to place it.
Wait for the list to settle. You can also reorder from the narrow project list while an editor is open, when search is clear.
Click Publish site to make the new portfolio order live.
check: The moved work stays in its new CMS position. After deployment, the public portfolio follows that order.
notes: Project list moves save automatically. There is no Sort order field to edit in the form.
Publishing an order change does not require editing the project content. Dragging is disabled while searching or selecting multiple items.
An accidental saved move can be corrected by dragging the work back before publishing.

chapters.text: To reorder the portfolio, open the Projects table. Clear search and leave selection mode first.
Drag the grip at the far left of a project row. Release at the insertion line for the new position.
The move saves automatically. Review the new order before continuing.
Click Publish site to make the order live. Moving gallery rows is a separate procedure inside an individual project.

title: Duplicate a project
goal: Use an existing work as a starting point for a new entry.
steps: Open the source project and save it first, especially if it contains staged images.
Click Duplicate in the bottom toolbar. The copy opens immediately.
Rename the copy, review its new slug, and replace inherited text and images as needed.
Save the copy. Queue and publish it only when it is ready.
check: The new record is a draft with copy in its title and a distinct slug. The original is still present.
notes: Duplicate creates the new record immediately. Discard does not remove it.
Pending uploads are not copied. Save the original first if its staged images should carry over.
The copy references the saved image files from the original. Replace its image fields when it needs different media.

chapters.text: To duplicate a work, save the original first so its images are no longer pending.
Click Duplicate in the bottom toolbar. A new draft opens with copy added to its title and a distinct slug.
Rename the new work and review all inherited text and images before saving.
The original stays in place. Queue and publish the copy only when the new entry is ready.

title: Save work as a draft
goal: Keep an incomplete project out of the publish queue.
steps: Open a new or existing draft and make your edits.
Open More publish options, the arrow beside Queue to publish.
Choose Save as draft. The record is saved with the status Not published.
Reopen it to continue editing. Use Queue to publish when the required fields are complete.
check: The status reads Not published and the edits remain after reopening.
notes: Save stores edits but preserves the current workflow where possible. Use Save as draft when you specifically need Not published.
On an already published item, Save as draft changes its publication status. Use this deliberately and rebuild the live site if it should disappear.

chapters.text: To keep an incomplete work as a draft, make your edits in the project editor.
Open the arrow beside Queue to publish. Choose Save as draft.
The status changes to Not published. Your saved edits remain available when you reopen the record.
When the work is complete, use Queue to publish. Be deliberate when applying draft status to a work that is already live.

title: Queue changes and publish the site
goal: Release completed content and ordering changes to the public website.
steps: Finish editing the item. Click Queue to publish and wait for saving or image uploads to finish.
Review the intended queued records across Projects and Pages. Publish site acts globally, including other queued items and pending project order changes.
Click Publish site in the top bar. Watch the notification while the deployment is queued and building.
Wait for Deployed and Your site is live. Open the public website, refresh it, and verify the changed text, images, or order.
If publishing fails, follow the error message. The CMS attempts to restore affected content and ordering so they can be retried.
check: The deployment reaches Deployed and the intended result is visible on the public website.
notes: Save and Queue to publish do not by themselves rebuild the public website. The website is generated during deployment.
Publish site is shown when there are queued records, pending order changes, or a retry. It does not publish only the currently open record.
The training clip simulates deployment states. It demonstrates the UI without triggering a real website deployment.
If the message says Still deploying, check with the administrator before retrying. Deploy triggered alone does not confirm that a build has completed.

chapters.text: To release a finished item, click Queue to publish. This saves the content and uploads any staged images.
Publish site acts on all queued content and pending project order changes. Check the other queued work before proceeding.
Click Publish site in the top bar. Watch the deployment notification as the website is queued and built.
Wait for Deployed and Your site is live. This training copy simulates those states; it does not deploy the real website.
On the real site, refresh the public page and check the result. If a deployment fails or keeps building, follow the message and contact the administrator if needed.

title: Unpublish a project
goal: Hide a work without deleting its saved content.
steps: Open the published project you want to remove from public view.
Open More publish options and choose Unpublish.
Check that the status changes to Not published. The record stays in the CMS.
Rebuild the website using Publish site. If that button is absent, queue a complete item that should remain visible, then publish, or ask the administrator to rebuild the site.
check: After a successful deployment, the work is absent from the public portfolio but remains editable in the CMS.
notes: Unpublish is available for Published records. It is not a deletion.
The old public page can remain visible until the next successful build. Unpublishing alone may not show Publish site.

chapters.text: To hide a published work while retaining its content, open the project and then More publish options.
Choose Unpublish. The record stays in the CMS with the status Not published.
The public website needs a new build. If Publish site is absent, queue a complete item that should remain visible, then publish, or ask the administrator to rebuild.
After deployment, check that the work is gone from the public portfolio. You can queue it again later to republish it.

title: Delete a project
goal: Permanently remove an unwanted project record.
steps: Open the project and verify its title. Export a copy first if you need a reference.
Click Delete in the bottom toolbar.
Read the confirmation and click Delete only when the record is correct. Cancel leaves it in place.
If the work was live, rebuild the website. If Publish site is absent, queue a complete item that should remain visible and publish, or ask the administrator to rebuild.
check: The record is absent from Projects. After deployment, it is absent from the public portfolio.
notes: The confirmation states that deletion cannot be undone. There is no trash or restore interface.
For a temporary removal, use Unpublish instead. Fixed Pages and Site Settings have no Delete control.
CSV export preserves record values and image URLs, not an independent backup of the image files.

chapters.text: To permanently remove a project, open it and check the title carefully.
Click Delete in the bottom toolbar. The confirmation says this cannot be undone. Cancel if you selected the wrong record.
Confirm Delete. The project disappears from the CMS list.
If the work was public, rebuild the website as well. Use the publishing procedure or ask the administrator for a rebuild if Publish site is absent.

title: Edit a fixed page
goal: Update text and images on About or the essay page.
steps: Choose Pages and open the page you want to change.
Edit Body using the rich text toolbar. Use Heading 2 or Heading 3 for subsections, and the list or link controls as needed.
Update Image or SEO settings if required. Keep the existing slug for fixed pages unless the administrator has arranged a routing change.
Click Save or Queue to publish, then Publish site when the page is ready.
check: The saved text is correct in the editor. After deployment, the intended fixed page shows the update.
notes: Pages is a fixed collection: you can edit the existing pages but cannot add, duplicate, import, or delete them here.
The editor does not provide a general page section builder. Add or remove paragraphs and headings within Body. Structural layout changes need development work.
Use Undo in the text toolbar for recent typing. Discard reloads the entire record from its last save.

chapters.text: To change a fixed page, choose Pages and open the page you need.
Edit the Body field. The toolbar supports headings, emphasis, lists, and links, and lets you add or remove text sections within the body.
Check the page image and keep the existing slug. Fixed pages cannot be added or deleted from this CMS.
Click Save or Queue to publish, then Publish site when the page is ready. Check the result on the public page after deployment.

title: Update site settings
goal: Change the site identity and public contact details.
steps: Choose Site Settings. Its single record opens directly.
Edit Name, Tagline, Location, Email, Phone, Description, or the default Social image as needed.
Click Save and wait for any uploads to complete.
Arrange a site rebuild so the saved settings appear publicly. If Publish site is absent, queue a complete content item that should stay visible and publish, or ask the administrator to rebuild.
check: The saved settings remain after reopening. After deployment, public identity and contact details show the intended values.
notes: Site Settings uses Save and has no per record publication controls. Saving it alone does not create a queued content item.
The Email and Phone fields are public website contact details. They do not change your editor login.
The default Description and Social image are used when a page has no more specific value.

chapters.text: To change site wide details, choose Site Settings. The single settings record opens directly.
Update the name, tagline, location, public email or phone, and default sharing information as needed.
Click Save. These public contact fields do not change your editor login.
The static website picks up saved settings during its next build. If Publish site is absent, queue a complete item that should remain visible and publish, or ask the administrator to rebuild.

title: Change search and sharing details
goal: Set the page title, description, and image used for search and link previews.
steps: Open the relevant project or page and scroll to SEO settings.
Enter Meta title and Meta description if the normal title or default summary is unsuitable.
Add or replace Social image if this page needs a specific link preview image.
Click Save or Queue to publish, then Publish site. Check the public page after deployment.
check: The saved SEO fields match the intended title, summary, and sharing image.
notes: Empty Meta title falls back to the item title. Empty image fields use the configured page, project, or site defaults.
Search engines and social services may cache older previews; their results may update after the website itself.
SEO fields describe the page for search and sharing. They do not replace the visible Body or Description.

chapters.text: To change search and sharing details, open the project or page and scroll to SEO settings.
Enter a clear Meta title and a short Meta description. Leave the title empty if the normal item title is already suitable.
Use Social image for a page specific sharing image. Save the record when the fields are ready.
Publish the site. Search engines and social networks may keep an older preview in their cache for a while.

title: Update several projects together
goal: Queue or change the status of several selected works.
steps: Choose Projects and return to the full table. Use Search first if it helps narrow the list.
Click Select, then click the rows you intend to change. Check the selection count; Select all selects the currently displayed records.
Open Update items and choose Queue to publish, Save as draft, or Unpublish as appropriate.
Click Cancel to leave selection mode. Review statuses and publish the site if the public website should change.
check: Only the selected rows have the intended status and no unrelated work was included.
notes: Bulk actions affect all selected records. Review the count and titles before applying a change.
Select mode also provides Export and, for Projects, Delete. Bulk deletion has a confirmation dialog.
Project dragging is disabled in Select mode. Leave that mode before reordering.

chapters.text: To change several projects together, open the full Projects table and click Select.
Click each row you want to include, then check the selected count and titles.
Open Update items and choose the intended status. Here, Queue to publish adds the selected works to the global publish queue.
Click Cancel to leave selection mode. Review the statuses, then use Publish site when the queued changes are ready.

title: Import projects from a CSV file
goal: Create project drafts from a prepared spreadsheet export.
steps: Prepare a CSV with a header row. Use column names such as title, slug, year, medium, description, and hero. Use accessible image URLs for asset fields.
Choose Projects, click Import, then Choose CSV file.
Review each Collection Field mapping. Match the relevant columns and leave unrelated columns at Ignore. Review the row count and any warnings.
Click Import rows. Open each imported draft, check its values and images, and complete required fields before queuing and publishing.
check: The imported works appear as Not published with the expected field values.
notes: Import creates new records; it does not update records with matching titles. Use unique slugs to avoid collisions.
The import is limited to 1000 rows per request. The internal project position is omitted from mappings; imported records append.
CSV import does not upload image binaries. A local file path is not a usable public image URL. Use the normal image controls if files still need uploading.
Pages and Site Settings do not offer Import.

chapters.text: To import project drafts, start with a CSV that has a header row and clear column names.
In Projects, click Import, then choose the CSV file.
Review the Collection Field mappings and the row count. Match the columns you need and leave other fields at Ignore.
Click Import rows. Import creates new drafts, so open and review each one before publishing. Image fields need accessible image URLs; local file paths do not upload images.

title: Export selected records
goal: Download record values as a CSV reference.
steps: Open Projects or Pages and use Search if needed.
Click Select and choose the rows to export. Use Select all for the currently displayed records.
Click Export to download the CSV.
Open the file to confirm the rows and columns. Click Cancel to leave selection mode.
check: A CSV file downloads with the selected records and their field values.
notes: The export contains image URLs and gallery data, not the image files themselves. Keep master media files separately.
An export is useful as a reference. Import creates new records, so reimporting an export is not a restore or update procedure.

chapters.text: To export records, open the collection table and click Select.
Choose the rows you need. Select all applies to the currently displayed records, including any search filter.
Click Export. The browser downloads a CSV containing the selected values.
Check the downloaded file, then click Cancel to leave selection mode. Images are represented by URLs; the media files are not included.

title: Discard edits and sign out
goal: Leave the CMS with saved work accounted for.
steps: Check Unsaved beside the editor controls. Click Save if you want to keep the edits.
To abandon local edits, click Discard. This reloads the entire record from the last saved version.
If you navigate away with edits, choose Cancel to keep editing or Discard to leave without saving.
Click your editor name at the top right to sign out. Confirm the login screen returns.
check: The login screen is visible and no wanted changes were left unsaved.
notes: Discard only affects unsaved field edits. It does not undo a saved record, a project list reorder, a deletion, or the immediate creation of a record.
If a conflict says the item changed elsewhere, copy any text you need, reload the record, review the latest version, and reapply your changes.
If your session expires, sign in again before retrying a save. Avoid closing the tab while uploads are running.

chapters.text: Before leaving the CMS, check whether the editor shows Unsaved.
Click Discard only if you want to reload the entire record from its last save. Saved changes and automatically saved project ordering are not undone.
Once your work is saved or discarded, click your editor name at the top right to sign out.
The login screen returns. If you need to keep working later, sign in again with your editor account.
